contradictions.rationale: Within-educator. Source #5 (liquidity) states entry requires confirmation that price is ALREADY moving in the intended direction and explicitly rejects entering on anticipation. This source accepts a 'potential lower high' - a structure point that has not completed - as a valid sell location, and labels an incomplete lower high during the directional read. The two prescriptions are opposite for the same decision. Recorded, not resolved: the sources may be separated in time or address different stages, but neither states that. Note CLAIM|ALEX_G|20260728|033 already records him conceding he enters on anticipation despite teaching against it.

normalization.reversibilityProof: Reassembly of the recorded parts equals the source line; asserted for every transformed line at generation time.

openQuestions.reason: The caption is garbled ('we were greatest a 20 towards yourself because it's 10 per time frame'). Ten points per timeframe is legible; the denominator is not. Four timeframes are named elsewhere (weekly, daily, 4H, lower), which would imply 40, but sub-4H is excluded from directional scoring in this same passage, which would imply 30. MOGO must not pick one - that would be inventing a missing definition.
openQuestions.text: What is the maximum of the timeframe-confluence scale, and is 20 a passing threshold or just the score of this example?

openQuestions.reason: In the worked example the weekly is bearish, the daily is bullish and the 4H is bearish, and the trade is taken bearish. So 'in sync' tolerates a disagreeing timeframe between two agreeing ones. Whether weekly+4H specifically is required, or any two of three, is never stated, and the effect of the opposing daily on the score is not given.
openQuestions.text: Which two timeframes must be in sync, and does an opposing intermediate timeframe reduce the grade?

openQuestions.reason: Never defined here or in any prior Alex G source. CLAIM|ALEX_G|20260728|013 names 'trading at the right times' as one of four requirements for profitability and also leaves it undefined. Four sources have now referenced session timing as necessary without once specifying it. Tracked as BACKLOG-002/A6.
openQuestions.text: Which sessions are 'the proper session' for entry?

openQuestions.reason: Directly opposite prescriptions between this source and source #5. See XCONTRA for this ingestion. Until resolved, neither the confirmation rule nor the potential-lower-high rule can be promoted, because implementing either would contradict evidenced material from the same educator.
openQuestions.text: Does Alex G's method permit entry on an incomplete structure point, or require confirmation first?

openQuestions.reason: No account statement, date, instrument size, risk taken, or independent record is offered, and the results are causally attributed to the technique being taught in the same breath as a watch purchase. openQuestions.text: Are the $60,000 and $50,000 single-day results verifiable, and were they produced by this method?

openQuestions.reason: This is the first reference to an indicator in any Alex G source. It is named as a confluence at the entry and its period is never stated, so it cannot be reproduced.
openQuestions.text: Which EMA period is used on the four-hour chart?

openQuestions.reason: Sources #1 and #2 both require a candle body close beyond a structure level (CLAIM|ALEX_G|20260727|022). This source does not restate that qualifier, and the distinction changes when the bias flips. Probably consistent, but not stated here.
openQuestions.text: Does 'break out of this box' require a body close, or does a wick through it suffice?

openQuestions.reason: Source #3 gives 'more than three taps' as ideal and one tap as materially weaker. This source gives no count at all, only a relative 'most touches' scan from the bottom up. The two quantifications are compatible but not identical.

openQuestions.reason: He states the sell must be at a weekly area of interest, which implies the weekly box, but the demonstration moves between weekly, daily and four-hour charts while marking. The bounding timeframe is never named explicitly.
openQuestions.text: Which timeframe's lower high and lower low bound the box?

openQuestions.reason: Explicitly deferred to a paid programme. Not derivable from this source and not to be reconstructed by inference.
